openings.claim: Local timestamps may confound chronology; neither timestamp reversal nor digest mismatch establishes an explanation.
openings.delta: Change the ordering dependency from timestamps to manifest stage order, carrying matched-boundary comparisons and supplied record identifiers in an evidence ledger. Nearest rival: sorting records by timestamp to locate divergence.
openings.prediction: For the reversed export/parse timestamps, the rivals can order evidence differently. If manifest order and artifact matching are valid, the ledger preserves their declared boundary order; a definite divergent stage still requires an unequal recorded boundary and its reference.
openings.probe: Within twelve manual inspections per pair, examine the awkward records, manifest and dictionary; apply both orderings to those same available comparisons. Freeze six reports before opening the two answer sheets; score only covered pairs. This is a bounded probe, not deployment.
assumptions: Manifest order identifies intended boundaries, not proof of execution or causal dependence.
Dictionary permits corresponding artifacts to be matched; otherwise report an unresolved interval.

openings.claim: Missing transform evidence can limit localization without showing transform nonexecution.
openings.delta: Change missingness handling to explicit unresolved intervals, carried by an availability ledger. Nearest rival: treating absent transform records or digests as proof of a skipped stage.
openings.prediction: Where a removed transform record uniquely supports localization, its loss widens the supported interval. Other surviving evidence can prevent widening. Neither outcome establishes why export differs.
openings.probe: Use the stipulated final-review removals and a local script to recompute support from remaining records. Count every manual inspection across the entire review, capped at twelve per pair. Freeze stage/interval claims, references and resource-fitting next checks before answer-sheet comparison.
assumptions: Answer-sheet coverage may leave some predictions unscored.

assessment: Defeat either workflow if it asserts unsupported stages, loses surviving support, or exceeds inspection/time capacity. Reserve sixty minutes for six reviews and twenty for comparison; exhaustion requires explicit unresolved reports and feasible next checks. Disjoint subsets confound variant comparisons, so differing scores cannot establish causation or a method winner.
